## Intent

**Problem:** A capture write (Epic 3) is a blocking round trip with no trace on Meus Registros: a failed write vanishes silently (only the capture modal's own local error shows), and nothing on a listed card tells the user whether what they wrote is actually saved server-side.

**Approach:** Introduce one shared in-memory `PendingEntryWriteTracker` domain port that the three capture cubits and `MeusRegistrosCubit` both consume. Capture cubits route `create()` through it (optimistic pending record before the call, resolved/failed after); `MeusRegistrosCubit` overlays the tracker's live pending writes on its confirmed list. One pure derivation function (`entries/domain`) computes each card's badge from `Entry.serverRevision`/`updatedAt` plus matching pending-write status, per `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`. Tapping an error badge retries through the same tracker when retryable; otherwise shows inline explanation only.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- New port + impl `entries/domain/services/pending_entry_write_tracker.dart` (pure Dart, RNF06 — no Flutter/data import; mirrors `SessionExpiryNotifier` pattern). API: `Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({required String content, required EntrySource source, int? mediaDurationSeconds})` (identical contract to `EntriesRepository.create()` today — capture cubits swap the dependency, no call-site logic change); `Future<void> retry(String tempId)`; `Stream<List<PendingEntryWrite>> get pendingWrites` — replay-capable (`Stream.multi` + cached last value, mirror `SessionRepositoryImpl.statusStream`, `session_repository_impl.dart:69-89`) so a late subscriber sees current pending state immediately.
- New value class `entries/domain/entities/pending_entry_write.dart`: `{tempId, content, source, mediaDurationSeconds, startedAt, status}`, `status` = `inFlight` or `failed(Failure)`. On `create()` success: tracker drops the record; `MeusRegistrosCubit` prepends the confirmed `Entry` into its own state (existing `_dedupedById` absorbs a later duplicate from `list()`). On failure: record flips `failed`, persists only in memory until `retry()` succeeds (no queued/offline write — UX-DR30, sync-badge.md: nothing survives restart).
- `create()` first drops any existing `failed`-status record before registering the new `inFlight` one (never more than one failed record at a time). Safe because exactly one Insertion Modal exists app-wide (one factory-scoped cubit, reset on each open — UX-DR26, UX-DR36), so there is only ever one "live" capture lineage: a user retrying by tapping "Salvar" again in the same still-open modal (not via the badge) must not leave the superseded attempt's error card as a permanent orphan on Meus Registros.
- One derivation fn `deriveSyncBadgeState(Entry? entry, PendingEntryWrite? pending)` in `entries/domain/entities/sync_badge_state.dart`, pure, returns sealed `SyncBadgeState` (`synchronizing | synchronized | error(Failure)`) (AD-10) — the only place this logic lives.
- Register tracker `lazySingleton` in `entries_injection.dart` (mirrors `MeusRegistrosCubit`'s own registration); inject into `TextEntryCubit`/`AudioEntryCubit`/`PhotoEntryCubit` (`capture_injection.dart`, replacing their direct `EntriesRepository.create()` call) and into `MeusRegistrosCubit` — constructor injection only, never cubit-to-cubit (AD-7).
- `EntryRecordCard` gains a badge (dot: `colorWarningSync`/`colorSuccess`/`colorError`, `design_tokens.dart:51,54,57`) + accessible label on tap/long-focus; retry hit area uses `DesignTokens.insertionModalTapTargetMin` (`design_tokens.dart:283`), scoped to the badge's own sub-widget only — the card itself stays non-tappable-for-navigation (Story 4.4's job).
- Tap on `error` badge: if `failure.retryable` (existing getter, `lib/core/failure/failure.dart`) call `tracker.retry(tempId)`; else render inline explanation text, no tap affordance.

**Ask First:** none — scope above is complete per investigation.

**Never:** persisting pending writes; a second retry endpoint (retry replays `create()` verbatim); any screen recomputing badge state inline; `EntryRecordCard` becoming navigation-tappable.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Fresh save | Capture cubit calls `tracker.create()` | Card appears top-of-today, ochre "Synchronizing" badge, before server responds | N/A |
| Write confirmed | `create()` resolves `Right(entry)` | Pending record removed, entry prepended, badge flips green "Synchronized" | N/A |
| Write fails, retryable | `create()` resolves `Left(networkTimeout)` | Card stays, red "Synchronization error" badge | Tap calls `tracker.retry(tempId)`, re-sends same payload |

# Step 2: Review

## RULES

- YOU MUST ALWAYS SPEAK OUTPUT in your Agent communication style with the config `{communication_language}`
- All review subagents must run at the same model capability as the current session.
- Run subagents synchronously: launch them together, then wait for all results before continuing.

## INSTRUCTIONS

1. The review layers are `{workflow.review_layers}`, resolved during activation.

2. For each layer in `{workflow.review_layers}`:
   - `instruction` empty or missing → drop the layer silently (an override disabled it).
   - `when` condition present and not satisfied by the current context (`{review_mode}`, `{spec_file}`) → drop the layer and tell the user, e.g. "Acceptance Auditor skipped — no spec file provided."
   - otherwise → the layer is active.

   If no layer is active, HALT with status `blocked` and blocking condition `no active review layers`.

3. Execute all active layers in parallel wherever their execution methods allow: expand `{skill-root}` in each layer's `instruction` to this skill's absolute installed directory, then substitute the runtime placeholders (`{diff_output}`, `{spec_file}`). For an instruction that launches a reviewer subagent, launch that child with the prompt text after placeholder substitution; do not load the reviewer instruction file yourself. For any other customized instruction, execute it as written. Do not leave `{skill-root}` unresolved in a child prompt. If a layer's instruction requires subagents and subagents are not available, for each such layer write under `{implementation_artifacts}` the exact child prompt from that layer's instruction after placeholder substitution (not a path-only pointer), then HALT. Ask the user to run each in a separate session (ideally a different LLM) and paste back the findings. When findings are pasted, treat them as those layers' findings and resume from this point. This is the only allowed parent-side read of a reviewer instruction file.

4. **Layer failure handling**: If any layer fails, times out, or returns empty results, append the layer's `name` to `{failed_layers}` (comma-separated) and proceed with findings from the remaining layers.

5. Collect all findings from the completed layers, keeping track of each finding's originating layer `id`.

   - `source` -- the `id` of the layer that produced the finding (e.g., `blind-hunter`), or merged sources joined with `+` (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`)
   - `title` -- one-line summary
   - `detail` -- full description
   - `location` -- file and line reference (if available)

2. **Deduplicate.** Deduplicate only findings with the same claim and same required action. If two or more findings meet both conditions, merge them into one:
   - Use the most specific finding as the base (prefer findings with a precise location over prose-only findings).
   - Append any unique detail, reasoning, or location references from the other finding(s) into the surviving `detail` field.
   - Set `source` to the merged sources (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`).

3. Then evaluate each remaining finding independently. Do not reject a finding because a related finding was rejected.

4. **Read the code before rating.** Before assigning severity, open the source at each finding's location and read enough surrounding code to judge reachability -- call sites, guards, and validation that live outside the diff hunk. Do not rate from the diff hunk alone. Severity reflects the real consequence at a real call site, not the worst theoretical reading.

5. **Assign severity** to each finding by consequence for the artifact's main consumer (software user, document reader, etc).
   Disregard any severity assigned by a reviewing subagent. Review subagents operate under by-design information asymmetry and do not have enough context to set final severity for this workflow.
   - `low` -- none or cosmetic
   - `medium` -- tolerable
   - `high` -- intolerable

6. **Route** each finding into exactly one triage bucket:
   - **decision_needed** -- There is an ambiguous choice that requires human input. The code cannot be correctly patched without knowing the user's intent. Only possible if `{review_mode}` = `"full"`.
   - **patch** -- Code issue that is fixable without human input. The correct fix is unambiguous.
   - **defer** -- Pre-existing issue not caused by the current change. Real but not actionable now.
   - **dismiss** -- Noise, false positive, or handled elsewhere.

   If `{review_mode}` = `"no-spec"` and a finding would otherwise be `decision_needed`, reclassify it as `patch` (if the fix is unambiguous) or `defer` (if not).

7. **Drop** all `dismiss` findings. Record the dismiss count for the summary.

8. If `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, report which layers failed before announcing results. If zero findings remain after dropping dismissed AND `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, warn the user that the review may be incomplete rather than announcing a clean review.

9. If zero findings remain after triage (all rejected or none raised): state "✅ Clean review — all layers passed." (Step 3 already warned if any review layers failed via `{failed_layers}`.)

## NEXT

Read fully and follow `./step-04-present.md`

3	import '../../../../core/design_tokens.dart';
4	import '../../domain/entities/sync_badge_state.dart';
5	
6	/// `EntryRecordCard`'s own sync badge (Code Map) — a colored dot
7	/// ([DesignTokens.colorWarningSync]/[DesignTokens.colorSuccess]/
8	/// [DesignTokens.colorError]) plus its text label, always visible (not
9	/// hidden behind a tap). "Accessible label on tap/long-focus" is split
10	/// across two single-purpose widgets rather than two that both also
11	/// announce it: the dot's [Tooltip] (`excludeFromSemantics: true`) gives
12	/// the *visual* long-press popup only, while the one [Semantics] node
13	/// wrapping the whole badge (below) is the single accessibility
14	/// announcement on focus — code-review round 1 finding: a [Tooltip] left
15	/// at its default `excludeFromSemantics: false` injects its own semantics
16	/// label too, so pairing it with an outer [Semantics] of the same label
17	/// double-announced it to screen readers.
18	///
19	/// Only an [SyncBadgeError] badge is ever tappable (Boundaries): a
20	/// [Failure.retryable] one calls [onRetryTap] on tap (I/O matrix: "Tap
21	/// calls `tracker.retry(tempId)`, re-sends same payload"); a
22	/// non-retryable one instead toggles an inline explanation
23	/// ([SyncBadgeError.failure]'s own `message`) with no network call and no
24	/// retry affordance (Boundaries: "else render inline explanation text, no
25	/// tap affordance"). [SyncBadgeSynchronizing]/[SyncBadgeSynchronized] are
26	/// never tappable at all.
27	class SyncBadge extends StatefulWidget {
28	  const SyncBadge({required this.state, this.onRetryTap, super.key});
29	
30	  final SyncBadgeState state;
31	
32	  /// Called on tap only for a retryable [SyncBadgeError] — ignored (never
33	  /// even referenced) for every other state, and for a non-retryable
34	  /// error (Boundaries: "no tap affordance" there means no retry action,
35	  /// not no tap at all — tapping a non-retryable error still reveals its
36	  /// explanation, just never calls this).
37	  final VoidCallback? onRetryTap;
38	
39	  @override
40	  State<SyncBadge> createState() => _SyncBadgeState();
41	}
42	
43	class _SyncBadgeState extends State<SyncBadge> {
44	  bool _explanationExpanded = false;
45	
46	  @override
47	  void didUpdateWidget(SyncBadge oldWidget) {
48	    super.didUpdateWidget(oldWidget);
49	    // A retry attempt (or any other state transition) collapses a
50	    // previously-shown explanation — stale text from a superseded
51	    // failure should never linger once the badge has moved on (e.g.
52	    // synchronizing -> a *new* error after a retry that fails again).
53	    if (widget.state != oldWidget.state) {
54	      _explanationExpanded = false;
55	    }
56	  }
57	
58	  @override
59	  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
60	    final state = widget.state;
61	    final (color, label) = switch (state) {
62	      SyncBadgeSynchronizing() => (
63	        DesignTokens.colorWarningSync,
64	        'Sincronizando',
65	      ),
66	      SyncBadgeSynchronized() => (DesignTokens.colorSuccess, 'Sincronizado'),
67	      SyncBadgeError() => (DesignTokens.colorError, 'Erro de sincronização'),
68	    };
69	
70	    // Reuses the existing kanban color-dot token (8dp) rather than a new
71	    // literal (RNF08) — same shape/role (a small colored status dot), just
72	    // a different screen. `excludeFromSemantics: true` (Review finding):
73	    // the outer `Semantics(label: label)` below is this badge's one and
74	    // only accessibility announcement — this Tooltip exists purely for
75	    // its own visual long-press popup.
76	    final dot = Tooltip(
77	      message: label,
78	      excludeFromSemantics: true,
79	      child: Container(
80	        width: DesignTokens.kanbanDotSize,
81	        height: DesignTokens.kanbanDotSize,
82	        decoration: BoxDecoration(color: color, shape: BoxShape.circle),
83	      ),
84	    );
85	
86	    // `ExcludeSemantics` (Review finding): without it, the visible `Text`
87	    // below contributes its *own* implicit semantics label ("Sincronizando",
88	    // same string) that merges straight into the explicit `Semantics(label:
89	    // label)` container wrapping this whole row — doubling the announced
90	    // label even after the dot's own `Tooltip` was already excluded above.
91	    // The one `Semantics(label: label)` node is this badge's single source
92	    // of truth for its accessible text; this row is purely visual.
93	    final labelRow = ExcludeSemantics(
94	      child: Row(
95	        mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
96	        children: [
97	          dot,
98	          const SizedBox(width: DesignTokens.spacingXs),
99	          Text(
100	            label,
101	            style: DesignTokens.textMonoCaption.copyWith(color: color),
102	          ),
103	        ],
104	      ),
105	    );
106	
107	    if (state is! SyncBadgeError) {
108	      // `container: true` (Review finding) — without it, a `Semantics`
109	      // widget with no interactive descendant doesn't form its own node;
110	      // Flutter merges its `label` up into the nearest explicit container
111	      // ancestor instead (e.g. the Scaffold's own), so `label` alone is
112	      // never exactly what a screen reader (or `find.bySemanticsLabel`)
113	      // reports for this widget specifically.
114	      return Semantics(label: label, container: true, child: labelRow);
115	    }
116	
117	    final retryable = state.failure.retryable;
118	    return Semantics(
119	      label: label,
120	      container: true,
121	      button: true,
122	      child: InkWell(
123	        onTap: () {
124	          if (retryable) {
125	            widget.onRetryTap?.call();
126	          } else {
127	            setState(() => _explanationExpanded = !_explanationExpanded);
128	          }
129	        },
130	        child: ConstrainedBox(
131	          constraints: const BoxConstraints(
132	            minWidth: DesignTokens.insertionModalTapTargetMin,
133	            minHeight: DesignTokens.insertionModalTapTargetMin,
134	          ),
135	          child: Align(
136	            alignment: Alignment.centerLeft,
137	            child: Column(
138	              crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
139	              mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
140	              children: [
141	                labelRow,
142	                if (!retryable && _explanationExpanded)
143	                  Padding(
144	                    padding: const EdgeInsets.only(top: DesignTokens.spacingXs),
145	                    child: Text(
146	                      state.failure.message,
147	                      style: DesignTokens.textCaptionSm.copyWith(
148	                        color: DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary,
149	                      ),
150	                    ),
151	                  ),
152	              ],
153	            ),
154	          ),
155	        ),
156	      ),
157	    );
158	  }
159	}

Compilei os achados e verifiquei cada um no código real antes de classificar severidade. Resultado da triagem:

| # | Achado | Severidade | Bucket |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `create()` descarta *qualquer* escrita falhada pendente (não só a mesma linhagem/modal), perdendo o conteúdo sem replay | média | **defer** (já decidido deliberadamente no Spec Change Log da própria spec, round 1 — mas com justificativa mais estreita do que o código implementa) |
| 2 | `tracker.retry()` não tem guarda própria contra falha não-retentável — invariante só existe na UI (`SyncBadge`) | baixa | patch |
| 3 | Nenhum teste exercita o caminho completo tap no badge → `MeusRegistrosCubit.retry(entry.id)` pela tela real | média | patch |
| 4 | `loadFirstPage()` ignora `_pendingWrites` no branch de falha — card pendente/com erro desaparece até a próxima emissão | média | patch |
| 5 | `EntryRecordCard`/`SyncBadge` sem `key` na lista — estado local pode vazar entre cards ao trocar posição | baixa | patch |
| 6 | Placeholders pendentes renderizam do mais antigo pro mais novo, invertido vs. convenção "mais novo primeiro" | baixa | patch |
| 7 | `_dedupedById` muta o `seenIds` do chamador por referência (inofensivo hoje, efeito colateral não documentado) | baixa | patch |

**11 achados descartados como ruído** (verificados e refutados): token `colorWarningSync` já existia antes do diff; teste novo em `entries_repository_impl_test.dart` cobre código pré-existente inalterado; teste "AC3 scroll position" é scope bleed não relacionado; assimetria `retry()`/`create()` sem consumidor real; a "race" entre streams já é neutralizada pelo próprio design (snapshot pós-remoção + dedup local síncrono); falta de timeout no write pendente já é mitigada pela infra de timeout do Dio; `repository.create()` lançar exceção violaria o contrato RNF09 já estabelecido em toda a base, não é regressão deste diff; fragilidade do `badgeFor` é nota de qualidade, comportamento correto e testado; branch `_EmptyState` para `occurredAt` malformado é defensivo e estreito, já descartado pelo próprio Verification Gap; contradição textual na spec (Boundaries vs AC3/I-O matrix) é nota de documentação — o código já seguiu a leitura correta; nit de formatação de linha.

Vou gravar os achados na spec e então resolver o único item de `decision_needed`... — na verdade reclassifiquei o único candidato a decision_needed como `defer`, então não há itens pendentes de decisão. Vou escrever os achados na spec agora.

  summary: `PendingEntryWriteTrackerImpl.create()` drops *any* existing `PendingEntryWriteFailed` record it's holding — not scoped to the same capture lineage/modal session — before registering a new `inFlight` write, silently discarding an unrelated previously-failed write's content with no way to replay it.

### Review Findings

- [ ] [Review][Patch] `tracker.retry()` has no internal `retryable` guard — invariant enforced only in `SyncBadge`'s `onTap`; add the same check inside `PendingEntryWriteTrackerImpl.retry()` for defense-in-depth [pending_entry_write_tracker.dart:180]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] No widget test exercises the full chain: tap a rendered error `SyncBadge` inside a real `MeusRegistrosScreen` → `MeusRegistrosCubit.retry(entry.id)`; a regression in `onRetryTap: (entry) => widget.cubit.retry(entry.id)` would ship undetected [meus_registros_screen.dart:109]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `loadFirstPage()`'s failure branch ignores `_pendingWrites` — unlike the success branch, it emits `MeusRegistrosError` unconditionally, hiding a pending/failed write's placeholder card until the next `pendingWrites` emission [meus_registros_cubit.dart:147]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `EntryRecordCard`/`SyncBadge` built with no `key:` in the per-day `for` loop — when list order changes (placeholder → confirmed entry swap), Flutter can reuse `SyncBadge`'s local `_explanationExpanded` state across a different card at the same position [meus_registros_screen.dart:277]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `_displayEntries` prepends `pendingWrites` oldest-first among themselves, inverted relative to the newest-first convention `groupEntriesByDate` documents its callers must follow; with 2+ concurrent pending writes the older one renders above the newer one [meus_registros_state.dart:980]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `_dedupedById` mutates the caller-supplied `seenIds` set in place when one is passed — harmless today (the one caller discards it afterward) but an undocumented side effect [meus_registros_cubit.dart:259]

### Review Findings

- [x] [Review][Patch] `tracker.retry()` has no internal `retryable` guard — invariant enforced only in `SyncBadge`'s `onTap`; add the same check inside `PendingEntryWriteTrackerImpl.retry()` for defense-in-depth [pending_entry_write_tracker.dart:180] — fixed: `retry()` now checks `failedStatus.failure.retryable` itself before replaying.
- [x] [Review][Patch] No widget test exercises the full chain: tap a rendered error `SyncBadge` inside a real `MeusRegistrosScreen` → `MeusRegistrosCubit.retry(entry.id)`; a regression in `onRetryTap: (entry) => widget.cubit.retry(entry.id)` would ship undetected [meus_registros_screen.dart:109] — fixed: added `meus_registros_screen_test.dart`'s new "retry wiring (spec-4-2, screen-level)" group with a controllable tracker fake.
- [x] [Review][Patch] `loadFirstPage()`'s failure branch ignores `_pendingWrites` — unlike the success branch, it emits `MeusRegistrosError` unconditionally, hiding a pending/failed write's placeholder card until the next `pendingWrites` emission [meus_registros_cubit.dart:147] — fixed: the failure branch now mirrors the success branch's `_pendingWrites` overlay.
- [x] [Review][Patch] `EntryRecordCard`/`SyncBadge` built with no `key:` in the per-day `for` loop — when list order changes (placeholder → confirmed entry swap), Flutter can reuse `SyncBadge`'s local `_explanationExpanded` state across a different card at the same position [meus_registros_screen.dart:277] — fixed: added `key: ValueKey(entry.id)`.
- [x] [Review][Patch] `_displayEntries` prepends `pendingWrites` oldest-first among themselves, inverted relative to the newest-first convention `groupEntriesByDate` documents its callers must follow; with 2+ concurrent pending writes the older one renders above the newer one [meus_registros_state.dart:980] — fixed: iterates `pendingWrites.reversed`.
- [x] [Review][Patch] `_dedupedById` mutates the caller-supplied `seenIds` set in place when one is passed — harmless today (the one caller discards it afterward) but an undocumented side effect [meus_registros_cubit.dart:259] — fixed: now builds a local copy (`{...?seenIds}`) instead of reusing the caller's set.
